Project Prometheus · UBS-6 · wireframe album

Shop — the full transaction lifecycle, drawn at ten viewports

Nine lifecycle states of one shop visit, each drawn at every ratified viewport plus 1080p, 1440p, 4K and 4K at 2× content scale. Compact composes as a single scrolling column, drawn both clipped and at full extent. Frames are rendered at true logical pixels against the published density tokens — click any frame to inspect it at 1:1.

113 frames · 9 states × 12 renders + 5 extents
Drawn to TSV-1..9, EPUX-13..17, UUI-1..19
Compact drawn twice — UUI-12 occlusion states
Status hypothesis, not an accepted UI contract

DEPENDENCY NOTE. UUI-15 held shop wireframes until an owner session, and TSV-10..24 — selector ownership, stacking, disabled rows, drag, destination timing, overflow, receipts, reversal, error contract — are still open. Four of them were ruled in session to unblock this album: quantity steppers appear only on infinite-stock unstateful items; destination is fixed to the inherited subject with silent convoy overflow; the viewport set adds 1440p, 4K and 4K at 2× content scale; and Compact is drawn in both occlusion states. Everything else follows the register's own recommendation and is marked as such.

01Entry — the checkpoint is taken

Opening the shop writes a temporary activity checkpoint before any transaction occurs. The subject is inherited from Explore, not asked for; the shop never opens with a “who is shopping?” prompt.

TSV-1..5EPUX-13EPUX-14UUI-16

What the frames show

  • The checkpoint is announced once, as status — it never steals focus.
  • Subject strip is present before the first row is read, so shopper-relative prices are never unexplained.
  • Buy is the landing tab; Sell is a sibling, not a separate activity.

03Selection — price formula and consequence preview

The selected item's description carries everything known about it: stats, effects, the full price breakdown with localized signed modifiers, and the consequences of its explicit action — resulting balance, destination, overflow.

TSV-6TSV-7TSV-8TSV-9EPUX-17

What the frames show

  • Base → signed modifiers → final. Never a raw formula string.
  • The action names the item and its cost. It is not a generic Buy bound to focus.
  • No quantity stepper here: Steel Lance carries durability, so it is stateful.
  • Destination is stated, not chosen — fixed to the inherited subject.

04Committed — one atomic transaction, appended to the visit

The transaction validated against live state and applied in full. Wallet, stock and destination all moved as one operation; the visit history grew by one line. There was no confirmation dialog, because the consequence is restorable.

TSV-2TSV-3TSV-5TSV-8TSV-12 (rec.)

What the frames show

  • Vulnerary is infinite-stock and unstateful, so the quantity stepper appears — ×2 fires two atomic transactions.
  • Convoy overflow happened silently and is reported after the fact, not negotiated before it.
  • Success is a status region, not a modal — routine updates never take focus.

07Exceptional consequence — a focused warning

Ordinary restorable actions commit without a second confirmation. This one does not: the instance is forged, so selling it destroys work that the visit checkpoint is the only thing standing behind. The dialog is bounded by the game view and renders at a fixed safe scale.

TSV-8UUI-5UUI-18TSV-21 (rec.)

08Exit review — Confirm Visit or Restore Checkpoint

Leaving after at least one successful transaction shows the visit history and asks for one whole-visit decision. Restore is not selective: there is no line-item undo, because there is no line-item receipt to reverse.

TSV-1..5TSV-9TSV-20 (rec.)TSV-22 (rec.)

What the frames show

  • Every transaction of the visit is listed with its own delta and destination.
  • The net position is stated in the wallet's own terms: 2,480 → 734.
  • Restore Checkpoint is the destructive option and is styled as such, not as Cancel.
  • Exiting with no transactions skips this surface entirely.

09Deep detail — an item carrying every function at once

The stress case. Sunder is forged three times, effective against two classes, carries two on-hit effects and two equipped passives, is gated behind three requirements, prices through four terms, and produces two consequences that need warning. Nothing here is a new surface — it is the same detail pane the simple items use, asked to carry everything.

10Two currencies — a shop that does not price in gold alone

The Ember Forge prices in gold plus two consumable materials. Nothing about the composition changes: one header figure, one control row, one list. The header shows the shop's declared primary currency, abbreviated, and rows lead with that same primary term so the scanned column stays consistent.

What the frames show

11Holdings — the currency figure is a button

Activating the header figure opens everything the player holds that a transaction could spend — currencies and consumable or transformable inventory alike. The list is unbounded, so it scrolls, and it carries full counts rather than the abbreviated glance.

Findings raised by drawing this

Five constraints that were not previously recorded. Each is visible in a frame above, marked FINDING.

  1. Docking the action bar inverted TSV-6, so Compact no longer docks anything. The first cut pinned the purchase button and the status bar to the bottom of the step while the content clipped above them — the action was reachable before its own cost was readable, which is the opposite of what TSV-6 exists to guarantee. Compact now composes as a single scrolling column: header and back strip stay, and everything below — stats, price, quantity, consequence, warnings, the action itself — is one unit that scrolls together. The action sits after the consequence by construction, not by reminder.
  2. The failure reason is the worst casualty of the fold. In the blocked state the shortfall figure sits below it. Whatever else scrolls, the reason a commit was refused must not.
  3. 852×393 is the tightest transaction surface, and the rail moved the constraint rather than removing it. SHC-4 turned the chrome 90°, taking the list from 3.6 to 7.0 rows — but a detail pane inside the 524-px rect is now 210px, narrower than the 240px it had before. Height was bought with width. The same 524px defeated six Settings tabs under UUI-19; three independent surfaces have now hit this number.
  4. The complex item killed the docked action everywhere — now a rule. Compact was rebuilt first, but Expanded still pinned the action to the bottom of the detail pane, and Sunder exposed what that costs: at 1024×768 and 1280×720 the pane clipped after Weapon triangle, so the price, the consequences and both warnings — including “cannot be sold, permanent for the campaign” — sat below the fold while the Buy button stayed permanently on screen. A player could commit an irreversible purchase the warning for which had never rendered. Ruled: single-scroll is the composition at every size class. The detail surface flows, the action is the last thing in it, and nothing is pinned beside content it contradicts. Consequence before action is then structural rather than a thing reviewers have to remember.
  5. 4K at 1.0 content scale is not a usable configuration. The 14px controller token is 0.36% of display height. The bounded workspace keeps the layout correct and unreadable at the same time, which is an argument for content_scale_factor defaulting by display size rather than to 1.0 — and that setting already carries reachability_risk under UUI-18.

Reading the frames

  • Dashed outline is the reserved control region — the game view's leftover, per UUI-1/2/3. Present on the four touch viewports, absent on desktop.
  • Single-scroll everywhere. Every detail surface flows and ends in its own action; nothing is docked. The hairline on a pane's right edge is the scroll thumb, and every extent quoted in a caption is measured from the rendered layout, not estimated.
  • The left column at Expanded is the shopper's character sheet, because the question in a shop is not what an item costs but what it does to this unit — so the sheet carries the equipped-weapon comparison for whatever is selected.
  • Dashed ring on a row is focus; filled with a left bar is selection. The two are never the same state — a highlighted row must never carry a generic buy action (TSV-8).
  • Hatched fill at 1440p and above is deliberate dead space. The workspace is bounded and centred; nothing stretches (UUI bounded-workspace rule).
  • Monospace values are metrics read from ResponsiveLayout.DENSITY_TOKENS, not invented.

What this album does not decide

  • TSV-10..24 remain open; frames drawn against a recommendation carry the ID in grey.
  • SHP-1..5 are still open in their own register — prices shown are illustrative.
  • Paint is not specified here. Under UUI-16 the shop sits inside the pack theme boundary, so every surface in these frames is repainted by the active pack.
  • No engine seam is proposed. ResourceLedger.quote/commit already exists; the checkpoint participant registry in TSV-3 does not.
